That's effectively $6.99 per pack, but this deal brings the box down to $169.99, or around $5.66 per pack instead.

articles.title: How One Crash Bandicoot Level Helped Build Naughty Dog
articles.summary: From a quick-fix solution to a triple-A staple, this is how an early Crash Bandicoot level inspired decades of cinematic level design in Uncharted and beyond.
body: As Leon Kennedy, we fled from a giant, mechanical statue. Eleven years later, we guided Nathan Drake and his brother, Sam, as they escaped from relentless pursuers on a motorbike. And recently, we helped forge a path through a literal wave of plague-infested rats for A Plague Tale’s Amicia. Three examples from literally hundreds of cinematic chase sequences in video games that can all trace their roots back to an unlikely source. The colourful cartoon platformer that started it all: Crash Bandicoot.

The running-towards-camera chase sequence is as popular now as it’s ever been, raising the cinematic tension in blockbuster games for the last 30 years. But its beginnings were humble, and its widespread use is all thanks to the Crash developers at Naughty Dog trying to solve a single problem: How do we show our character’s face more?

“It’s the modern Naughty Dog playing the antique Naughty Dog.” said Jason Rubin, a co-creator of Crash Bandicoot, in a 2019 interview with IGN. “What Nathan’s doesn’t understand is that this is basically the game that led to you. You exist because of this game!”
points: From a quick-fix solution to a triple-A staple, this is how an early Crash Bandicoot level inspired decades of cinematic level design in Uncharted and beyond.

articles.title: Castlevania Turns 40, And Konami May Have Just Teased A 3D Collection
articles.summary: Castlevania celebrated its 40th anniversary this week--an impressive milestone in video games and a terrifying pair of numbers for anyone who was born in 1987. Konami marked the occasion with a new video paying tribute to the original whip-slinging hero of the 1986 Famicom game, as well as all of…
body: Right near the end of the video, Castlevania's first protagonist, Simon Belmont, takes a quick stroll past a series of non-ruined portraits in Dracula's castle. Eagle-eyed observers will note that these feature cover art from three of the 3D-era games--Lament of Innocence, Curse of Darkness, and Lords of Shadow. The fourth one is for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, which launches in October 2026. Could Konami be teeing up a new compilation that bundles together the PS2 and Xbox 360/PS3-era 3D Castlevania games?

The company isn't saying anything, and there's a good chance that the games were chosen purely because they still have some of the best cover art in the franchise. They're pretty neat, artistically! But a Castlevania collection isn't uncommon, as Konami has released a few of these in the past. The Castlevania Anniversary Collection from 2019 collected eight games spanning the first 10 years of the series, and the Castlevania: Dominus Collection bundled all three DS-era games alongside the 1988 Haunted Castle arcade game.

articles.summary: Several years have passed since the last new Gears of War game was released, but at long last, that drought is almost over. Gears of War: E-Day will be one of the early highlights of October, and if you're looking to rev your Lancer up and turn back the Locust tide, you can start playing really…
body: According to the official PC requirements for Gears of War: E-Day, the game will require 115GB of storage capacity on that platform. Xbox Series X|S install sizes are typically on par with PC, so overall, you'll want to make sure you have at least 100GB of free space available on your machine. That's a pretty noticeable increase in size, as the previous game, Gears 5, required a chunky 80GB of space when it was first released back in 2019.
One other thing to note is that if you're planning to play on PC, the game requires a solid-state drive to be installed on. This is a mandatory requirement for the game to run optimally.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson’s New Cosmere Book Gets Exclusive New Reveal
articles.summary: Brandon Sanderson 's adult fantasy books are set in the sprawling Cosmere universe, where godlike beings fight for power on planets with their own complex rules for magic. The Mistborn series takes place in the world of Scadrial while The Stormlight Archive is set on Roshar.
body: The sheer number of interconnected books Sanderson has written can make getting into the Cosmere feel intimidating, but he’s created a solution in the Hoid’s Travails series. That began with the releases of Tress of the Emerald Sea and Yumi and the Nightmare Painter in 2023, the standalone books can be read in any order. The only connection to the vast Cosmere is Hoid, the storytelling trickster who appears in most of Sanderson’s works.

The next book in the series, The Fires of December, releases digitally on Oct. 6 and physically on Dec. 6. It was part of a BackerKit campaign last year for a Hoid’s Storybook Collection that raised $11 million. It’s the only Cosmere book the exceptionally prolific author is releasing this year as he focuses on the Mistborn film adaptation, co-writing the modern fantasy book Songs of the Dead, and continuing his YA sci-fi Cytoverse series with Blightfall.

articles.title: Arc Raiders announces a new PvE "test" to accommodate its surprisingly friendly players
articles.summary: Embark Studios has announced a new matchmaking test for Arc Raiders that'll allow players to opt into a PvE version featuring none of the usual player-versus-player violence.
body: In a blog post on the official Arc Raiders website, executive producer Aleksander Grøndal revealed the studio's PvE test will run from 13th to 20th October, and will enable participants to choose between the new, friendlier version of Arc Raiders and the regular, more ruthless version.

Grøndal goes on to recap Arc Raiders' origin as a raid-based co-op PvE shooter with looting mechanics, and Embark's eventual decision to shift towards the extraction shooter we know today. However, in an interesting twist of fate, it turns out many players are approaching the game with a collaborative mindset despite the incentives to kill their fellow players, turning it into what Grøndal calls the "Extraction (Don’t) Shooter".

He further breaks down this phenomenon with statistics, highlighting that around 37 percent of raiders are friendly co-op players, and that this figure has grown since launch. In comparison, around 34 percent are PvP-focused - a figure that has stayed consistent since launch - and the remaining 27 or so percent of raiders are a mix between the two. So there's clearly demand for more formalised PvE.

articles.title: Ubisoft Was Working on an Official Legend of Zelda Game, Report Says
articles.summary: Ubisoft and Nintendo formed a partnership in the 2010s and early 2020s, resulting in 2017's crossover RPG Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle and its 2022 sequel. According to a new report, Ubisoft didn't want the partnership to be done there: Ubisoft Milan was reportedly working on a The Legend of…
body: Insider Gaming reported that Ubisoft Milan, co-developer of the Mario + Rabbids games, once pitched Nintendo on "an original Zelda spinoff starring a previously unknown protagonist." It called the project Goliath, "a name that reflected the scale of what Ubisoft Milan aimed to develop." Nintendo gave it the initial greenlight, but wanted Ubisoft to make Ganondorf the player character instead. The villainous Ganondorf is as essential to The Legend of Zelda series as Link and Zelda are, but is only playable in spinoff games like Hyrule Warriors and in the Super Smash Bros. games.

Ubisoft Milan worked throughout the year on a prototype, but Nintendo rejected that prototype in November. "The reasons for [Nintendo's] decision remain unclear," Insider Gaming said. It's also not clear what that prototype looked like or what type of game it would have been.

articles.title: Pokémon 30th Anniversary Jirachi Card Price Explodes After Tragic Death
articles.summary: For people who buy and sell Pokémon cards, the period right after a set releases is a chaotic one. Prices for illustration cards move in unpredictable ways, but the trend is almost always downward.
body: The reason is a sad one. Earlier in September, news broke that 12-year-old Pokémon influencer Avery The Poke Kid passed away after a prolonged fight against cancer. Avery's cheerful attitude, despite his trying circumstances, made him a beloved figure in the Pokémon community. Avery often featured in content where he encouraged people to cherish the cards they had, regardless of value. He also reminded people about the importance of living life to the fullest — and he did so in between chemotherapy sessions and surgeries.

Prior to passing away on Sept. 18, Avery's parents recorded a final video of him opening one more Pokémon pack. Much to his delight, the last pack he ever opened contained the Jirachi ex #155 card, illustrated by Akira Egawa. The bittersweet pack opening went viral, in part due to the significance of the card Avery pulled.

Prices for illustration cards move in unpredictable ways, but the trend is almost always downward.

articles.title: After nearly 19 years in development hell, Ubisoft's Beyond Good & Evil 2 is somehow still showing signs of life
articles.summary: Sound the alarm! Alert your loved ones! Nearly 18 years after its original announcement, Beyond Good & Evil 2 apparently still isn't dead, according to a Ubisoft Bordeaux developer who says he's been working on the game for months.
body: Beyond Good & Evil 2 was originally unveiled back in 2008, and has seemingly been stuck in development hell ever since. However, last year brought new signs of life when a fresh job posting for the game appeared online. And now, after another lengthy lull in updates, lead writer and associate narrative director Rik Godwin has confirmed (as spotted by IGN ) the project is still in development. With Ubisoft's permission, of course.
"Odd sort of non-announcement but for the past few months I've been working on Beyond Good & Evil 2 in a support/consultant role, Godwin wrote on social media. "I am allowed to say this, I checked."
The current state of Beyond Good & Evil 2 remains a mystery, and the overall question of whether it's dead or not has confounded onlookers for years.

articles.title: It took roughly two years and "one of the most expensive art assets ever" to get Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty's Chimera tank fight right
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has shared some insight into Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty 's fantastic Chimera tank boss fight, explaining it took two years to get the complicated sequence right.
body: In the latest episode of AnsweRED, the official CD Projekt Red podcast, game director Gabe Amatangelo and creative director Igor Sarzyński discussed the Chimera tank in a section focused on production challenges the team faced when making Cyberpunk 2077.

"Sometimes we're making content that's a nexus point of different disciplines - the Chimera is a great example of that," Amatangelo explained. "It was gameplay, narrative, art, worldbuilding. I remember [art director] Paweł Mielniczuk and I were sending each other emails of various different military equipment of those guns, what are those called? they go 'Brrrrrrrr' [imitating a big machine gun] We wanted it to terrify you when it came up."

In the end, said Mielniczuk a little later in the conversation, "We were doing the tank I think four times, changing equipment,the weapons." Sarzyński added: "One of the most expensive art assets I think ever."

articles.title: GTA veteran's MindsEye studio Build a Rocket Boy has entered administration, following yet more reports of layoffs
articles.summary: Last week brought reports of further layoffs at Build A Rocket Boy, the beleaguered studio behind the poorly received 2025 shooter MindsEye. In the wake of that news, the company - which has repeatedly attempted to blame its woes on 'sabouteurs' - has filed for administration.
body: Build A Rocket Boy was founded in 2016 by GTA veteran Leslie Benzies, and its first game, Everywhere, was announced in 2022. Everywhere was envisaged as a user-generated content platform promising to redefine "how players connect with one another and the digital world around them". But along the way, MindsEye - initially unveiled as a component of Everywhere - evolved into a standalone "AAA" game that eventually released last June.

On release, however, the game was panned by both critics and players, and studio CEO and CTO Mark Gerhard would later describe its arrival as "without doubt, the worst launch in history". Soon after MindsEye's arrival, the layoffs began and more followed earlier this year, with Gerhard blaming the studio's woes on "organised espionage and corporate sabotage". It's a narrative he has repeatedly returned to, even as he pledged continued support for the game in June, insisting "people had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product".
points: Last week brought reports of further layoffs at Build A Rocket Boy, the beleaguered studio behind the poorly received 2025 shooter MindsEye.
